AfterObtained.rationale: SETTLED by the 2026-07-26 relic fix pass; this entry previously filed a gap because the auditor could not see whether `RunState.add_card` appends. It does, and both sides append at the same end. C#: ArcaneScroll.cs:27 is `CardPileCmd.Add(card, PileType.Deck)`, the no-index overload, which reaches `CardPile.AddInternal(card, index = -1)` (src/Core/Entities/Cards/CardPile.cs:83-97) whose own parameter doc at CardPile.cs:80 says '-1 will cause it to be added to the end ("bottom")' and whose `else` arm is `_cards.Add(card)` (CardPile.cs:96). Sim: sts2_rl/relics/arcane_scroll.py:31 calls `run.add_card(make_card(pick))`, and sts2_rl/run.py:349 is `self.deck.append(card)` -- the END of the deck. Same placement. The sim ALSO runs the two deck-add hooks the source runs around it: `modify_card_being_added_to_deck` before the append (sts2_rl/run.py:345-348, the Hook.ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck analogue the egg relics use) and the deck arm of AfterCardChangedPiles after it (sts2_rl/run.py:351-353). Six other relic records already verdict this exact mechanism faithful -- relic/storybook N1, relic/tanxs_whistle N1, relic/sere_talon N5, relic/neows_bones N7, relic/dusty_tome N1 and relic/hefty_tablet N3 -- and storybook N1 names arcane_scroll's open question explicitly; leaving this one a gap was a rule-3 disagreement, not a finding. The old entry's 'LIVE as a documentation gap' framing is withdrawn: a record being under-cited is not something a player or a replay can see, so it was never a gap under the README's definition. Guard N5 below now carries the placement citation the entry was missing. Rule 7: src/Core/Entities/Cards/CardPile.cs and src/Core/Commands/CardPileCmd.cs are cited here; sts2_rl/run.py is already hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: CardRarityOddsType.Uniform + the `c.Rarity == CardRarity.Rare` filter + CardCreationFlags.NoUpgradeRoll (ArcaneScroll.cs:21) vs the sim's single player_rng.rewards.next_item over the Rare slice (arcane_scroll.py:28)
guards.rationale: Uniform odds mean no rarity draw is rolled and NoUpgradeRoll means no upgrade draw is rolled, so CreateForReward's whole RNG cost collapses to one NextItem over the filtered pool -- which is exactly what the sim spends, on the Rewards stream, matching the memory-of-record that relic and reward rolls burn PlayerRng.Rewards draws. CardsVar(1) (line 17) matches the sim's single pick, and both take element [0] of a one-element result.

The character pool, not a combat-filtered pool: the SP3 convergence work already established that reward generation draws from the full GetUnlockedCards rather than FilterForCombat, and pool_card_ids() is the sim's name for that same full pool. Recorded because using the combat-filtered pool here would be an easy and silent mistake.

guards.what: N3: the `if (list.Count > 0)` guard (ArcaneScroll.cs:24) vs the sim's `if rares:` (arcane_scroll.py:23)
guards.rationale: Both no-op when the pool yields nothing; neither can occur with the Ironclad pool, but the guards are structurally identical so no verdict rests on the unreachability.

guards.what: N4: HasUponPickupEffect is NOT overridden by ArcaneScroll.cs, and the sim correspondingly leaves has_upon_pickup_effect at its False default
guards.rationale: Checked explicitly because three other relics in this batch (alchemical_coffer, astrolabe, big_mushroom) DO override it and the flag drives Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:132), so getting it wrong changes which relics the trade events offer. ArcaneScroll.cs declares only Rarity, CanonicalVars and AfterObtained.

guards.what: N5 (added by the 2026-07-26 fix pass): the deck INSERTION POSITION, which the original AfterObtained entry could not settle from this record's two files
guards.rationale: Recorded as its own guard so the placement claim is pinned rather than buried in a hook rationale, and because it is the parity-critical half: audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json pins END placement for out-of-combat pile adds, and run.transform_card's docstring (sts2_rl/run.py:419-427) calls deck order out as parity-critical because the combat-start UnstableShuffle is order-dependent. Both sides append: C# `CardPileCmd.Add(card, PileType.Deck)` -> `CardPile.AddInternal(card, index = -1)` -> `_cards.Add(card)` (src/Core/Entities/Cards/CardPile.cs:90-97, doc at CardPile.cs:80); sim `run.add_card` -> `self.deck.append(card)` (sts2_rl/run.py:349). No divergence.
